text: Levan Makhashvili - Both the European Parliament's documents and the European Parliament itself have, unfortunately, lost their value - only a sporting interest remains: will they develop a document worse than the previous one, or will we have something new? (05.05.2026, 14:29)

"This document, along with its amendments which have made the initial version even more sharply worse, is completely detached from reality—for us and for the public, European Parliament documents and the European Parliament itself have unfortunately lost their value, as they do not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue," stated Levan Makhashvili, Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on European Integration, responding to the report on Georgia adopted by the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee.
According to him, today the European Parliament's agenda is not in alignment with the Georgia-EU agenda and, in general, with the agenda for Georgia's better, peaceful future.

"What can I tell you, you already know what we would do with this resolution [I would hand it in as waste paper] - for a simple reason: this document, along with its amendments which have made the initial document even worse, is completely detached from reality. Especially during these days and weeks, it is clearly visible who is actually hindering the dialogue. It is precisely the European Parliament, in the form of these specific political groups, which, based on their own narrow political agenda, are doing their utmost to obstruct the dialogue. If we look at the developments of previous years, this is exactly how it used to happen: whenever there was a prospect of resetting relations, dialogue, and cooperation, the European Parliament would swim completely against the current, and we are witnessing the same today."

"Therefore, for us and for society, both the European Parliament's documents and the European Parliament itself have unfortunately lost value, as they do not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue. Today, the European Parliament's agenda does not align with the Georgia-EU agenda and, in general, with the agenda for Georgia's better, peaceful future," stated Levan Makhashvili.

In response to the question that the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee is calling for sanctions against several Georgian media outlets in its adopted report, Makhashvili replied that these statements and entries in this specific document are laughable.

For information, the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee adopted a report on Georgia. In the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, 53 MEPs supported the annual report on Georgia, while 14 voted against it.
